blocks.orig: Whether you are experienced when it comes to safari tours or it is your first time: it is important to know exactly what you need to bring with you. Not only to get the most out of your safari in Tanzania, but also to make sure that you are as well-prepared for any possible situation that you might come across.
blocks.html: Whether you have been on plenty of safaris or this is your very first one, it pays to know precisely what to bring. Partly so you get the most out of your safari in Tanzania, but also so you are properly prepared for any situation you might run into.

blocks.orig: If you are struggling to think of absolutely everything that you will need to bring with you, have no fear, as we are here to help you out!
blocks.html: Finding it hard to think of absolutely everything you will need to take with you? Do not worry, because we are here to help you out!

blocks.orig: In this Tanzania safari packing list, we will go through all the items you need to take with you and explaining as to why you should bring them with you.
blocks.html: In this packing list for a Tanzania safari we run through every item you should take with you, and explain why each one belongs in your bag.

blocks.orig: This might seem like an obvious item to take with you, but it can be very easy to forget them if you are in a hurry. The documents and currency that you will need are as follows:
blocks.html: It may sound like an obvious thing to pack, yet documents are surprisingly easy to forget when you are rushing. These are the documents and the currency you will need:

blocks.orig: Passport: This is a no-brainer, but it can sometimes be tough to remember to pick up your passport on your way out of the door. Make a note about remembering your passport somewhere that you can be sure that you will see it- such as on the fridge or on the bathroom mirror- to help you keep it in mind. You will also need to make sure that your passport has a minimum validity of six months.
blocks.html: Passport: Obvious, of course, but actually picking up your passport on your way out of the door is something people genuinely do forget. Leave yourself a written reminder somewhere you are certain to see it, like the fridge door or the bathroom mirror, so it stays front of mind. You will also need to check that your passport remains valid for at least six months.

blocks.orig: Plane Ticket: Another obvious necessity, but again, it can be easy to forget them when you’re in a hurry.
blocks.html: Plane Ticket: Another clear essential, and yet again something that is easily left behind when you’re in a rush.

blocks.orig: Visa: E-visas are recommended as they can be ordered in advance, and they can be useful when it comes to avoiding any potential issues with obtaining a physical visa once you get to Tanzania. However, if it is necessary, they are available upon arrival in the country.
blocks.html: Visa: We recommend an e-visa, because you can arrange it in advance and it helps you avoid any possible trouble getting a physical visa once you land in Tanzania. If needed, though, visas are also issued on arrival in the country.

blocks.orig: Travel Insurance: This insurance will keep you covered for issues that might pop up during your trip to Tanzania, such as cancellations, flight delays, evacuations, theft, or loss of property, and any necessary medical expenses.
blocks.html: Travel Insurance: This cover protects you against problems that may crop up during your trip to Tanzania, such as cancellations, delayed flights, evacuations, theft or loss of belongings, and any medical costs you incur.

blocks.orig: Covid-19 documentation: As of January 2023 travellers can come in and out of the country without any Covid-19 documentation (vaccination and/or PCR-test).
blocks.html: Covid-19 documentation: Since January 2023 travellers can enter and leave the country without any Covid-19 paperwork (vaccination and/or PCR-test).

blocks.orig: Currency: It is best to be as prepared as possible when it comes to the money that you bring with you, so a mixture of debit or credit cards as well as cash is going to be your best bet. When it comes to what currency you are able to use in Tanzania, you can use US dollars so long as they are dated after 2006 as they are accepted in most major establishments in the country. You will also need to make sure that you have some Tanzanian shillings, as they will often be used in smaller establishments.
blocks.html: Currency: Be as well prepared as you can where money is concerned: a combination of debit or credit cards together with cash is going to be your safest option. As for which currency you are able to spend in Tanzania, US dollars are accepted in most of the major establishments in the country, provided the notes are dated after 2006. You will also want to make sure you carry some Tanzanian shillings, as the smaller establishments often work with those.

blocks.orig: Clothing can be a tricky element of a safari to pin down, as you never know exactly what you are going to get when it comes to the Tanzania weather.
blocks.html: Clothing is one of the harder parts of a safari to get right, because you can never be entirely sure what the Tanzania weather will do.

blocks.orig: Tanzania experiences both wet and dry seasons, with the dry seasons falling between January and February and then from June to October and the wet seasons lasting from March to May (this is the more prominent wet season) and then November and December.
blocks.html: Tanzania has both wet and dry seasons: the dry seasons run from January to February and again from June to October, while the wet seasons last from March to May (the more pronounced of the two) and then through November and December.

blocks.orig: For a safari in the dry season, you aren’t likely to see any rain, but it is best to pack a few jackets just to be sure.
blocks.html: On a dry-season safari you are unlikely to see rain, but it is wise to pack a few jackets just in case.

blocks.orig: Otherwise, light clothing will suffice. The wet seasons will call for heavier clothes, such as scarves and thicker jackets.
blocks.html: Beyond that, light clothing is all you need. The wet seasons call for heavier items, such as scarves and thicker jackets.

blocks.html: There are also some everyday clothes you will want to pack regardless of the season you travel in, including the following:

blocks.orig: As a whole, lightweight outfits in neutral colors are a practical choice for a safari, but remember that layering is your best friend!
blocks.html: Overall, lightweight outfits in neutral colours are the practical choice for a safari, but keep in mind that layers are your best friend!

blocks.orig: You might be doing a fair amount of walking during your safari (especially if it is a walking safari specifically) and so comfortable footwear is a must.
blocks.html: You may well do a fair bit of walking during your safari (certainly if it is specifically a walking safari), so comfortable footwear is essential.

blocks.orig: A pair of sneakers that you are willing to let get dirty is a great idea, whilst hiking boots that are sturdy and offer a great deal of ankle support are also a necessity.
blocks.html: A pair of trainers you do not mind getting dirty is a good idea, while sturdy hiking boots with plenty of ankle support are a must as well.

blocks.orig: If you are planning on doing some relaxing at the beach as well as embarking on your safari, don’t forget your flip-flops or sandals!
blocks.html: If you intend to combine your safari with some time relaxing on the beach as well, do not forget to pack your flip-flops or sandals!

blocks.orig: A basic first aid kit will help to avoid any unexpected mishaps or illnesses on your safari.
blocks.html: A basic first aid kit helps you deal with any unexpected mishaps or illness during your safari.

blocks.orig: From regular painkillers to medications to avoid sickness and diarrhoea – you want to make sure that you are stocked up on the essentials. This way, you can continue to enjoy your trip even if you have to deal with any medical problems.
blocks.html: From ordinary painkillers to medication against nausea and diarrhoea – make sure you are stocked up on the essentials. That way you can keep enjoying your trip even if a medical problem comes up.

blocks.orig: Even the smallest first aid kit will suffice, as long as you have the right tools to deal with any cuts, bruises, or reactions that might occur!
blocks.html: Even the tiniest first aid kit will do, provided it contains what you need to treat any cuts, bruises or reactions that might occur!

blocks.orig: You will also need to keep in mind that you are going to be outside for a long period of time whilst on safari, so protection from the sun is crucial.
blocks.html: Bear in mind as well that you will be spending long stretches of time outdoors while you are on safari, which makes protection from the sun vital.

blocks.orig: As well as sunscreen, bring some after-sun lotion as well.
blocks.html: Besides your sunscreen, pack some after-sun lotion as well.

blocks.orig: As well as your phone, there is no doubt that you will want to capture the moments you experience during your safari, so a camera is sure to be on your list of essential items.
blocks.html: Apart from your phone, you will certainly want to record the moments you experience on safari, so a camera is bound to be on your list of essentials.

blocks.orig: Don’t forget the charger for your camera (that goes for your phone too!) and spare batteries, as well as an extra memory card. Universal plug converters and binoculars are a must too!
blocks.html: Remember the charger for your camera (and for your phone!), spare batteries and an extra memory card. Universal plug adapters and binoculars are essential as well!
